## Historical audit — S0146

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C2/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 3 is visible. Citations below identify JSONL events and the supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal and construction | The requested goal was an editable, single-photo indoor reconstruction. The student interpreted the scene as a metalworking workshop and coded architecture, a bench, multiple lathes and wheels, an anvil, drawer, containers and tools. These object identities and image bounds are the student’s hypotheses, not independently viewed facts. [line 15, student `model_request` history, chars 0–243755) |
| Objects and connections | The code creates multiple semantic assets and nested wheel, lathe and bench parts, with explicit support coordinates. Step 2 changes the lathe builder to return the attached node before adding wheels. This is evidence of intended ownership, not a geometric test of connections, collision or support. [line 15, chars 0–243755) |
| Camera and pose | After step 1, the student estimated a shallow bench and low, undersized wheel and changed camera position and target while retaining the 39 mm lens. The revision also changed the attached-node handling, so it was not strictly camera-only despite its stated intention. The student later estimated residual sill-slope and container-crop differences. [line 15, chars 0–243755); line 17, student `model_response`, chars 0–18659) |
| Materials and lighting | The programs use distinct wood, iron, blue and plaster colors, plus scoped procedural noise/bump on architecture and bench. The student hypothesized that broad illumination washed out several surfaces, then reduced world strength from .32 to .10 and emitter powers from 1150/280 to 260/35. That was an executed lighting revision, not proof of its visual effect or the material identities. [lines 15, 17–18, respectively chars 0–243755), 0–18659), 0–19307) |
| Validation and outcome | Steps 1 and 2 are reported as valid renders, with execution elapsed times 42.891 and 46.881 seconds. Step 3 executed and returned `ok: true`, a saved render and blend file; the trace then records two selections of step 3. This establishes operational rendering and selection, not formal visual or geometric success. [line 15, chars 0–243755); line 18 `execute`, chars 0–19307); line 19 `execution_result`, chars 0–93251); lines 20–21 `select`, chars 0–59) each] |
| Input and exploration | The visible input includes task procedure, render-comparison prompts and scheduling evidence; no separately identified teacher diagnosis or teacher message appears in this chunk. The student independently proposed camera and lighting revisions in response to those prompts. The recorded third student session had zero tool calls and a read-only sandbox; execution was a separate runner event. Receipt or adoption of unseen teacher input is unknown. [line 15, chars 0–243755); line 16 `codex_session`, chars 0–3827); lines 17–18] |

**Assessment and uncertainty.** This is a nonempty, operational reconstruction with successful render events; overall correctness and final visual quality remain **unknown**, not established success or algorithm failure. The images themselves are not visible to this audit. In particular, wheel pose, actual part attachment and support, object visibility, texture fidelity, camera alignment and whether the darker lighting helped remain unresolved. A transferable observation is that separating camera and appearance revisions makes hypotheses easier to inspect, but successful execution alone validates neither. The particular anchor estimates and lighting values are task-specific hypotheses, not general calibration rules.
